components.note: 纟 (thread) — 纷 originally described tangled threads, extended to mean things scattered or in disorder.
分 (fēn) is an exact match for the sound of 纷.

example.fact: 纷 commonly appears in 纷纷 (fēnfēn, "one after another, in profusion"), often describing many things happening or falling at once.

meanings: to trim (a border with braid, tape etc)

components.note: 氵 (water) — 沿 originally meant following the edge of a river, later extended to 'along' any path or course.

example.fact: 沿 is often paired with 着 to form 沿着 (yánzhe, "along"), commonly used for directions like walking along a street or river.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 喊 describes an action made with the mouth, shouting.
咸 (xián) gives a sound distantly related to hǎn, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā dàshēng hǎn wǒ de míngzi.
example.fact: 喊 is the everyday verb for "to shout" or "to call out," often paired with 大声 (dàshēng, "loudly").

components.note: 辶 (to walk) — 违 involves stepping away from what is required, i.e. disobeying.
韦 (wéi) is an exact match for the sound of 违.

example.fact: 违 rarely stands alone — it usually appears in words like 违反 (wéifǎn, "to violate") or 违法 (wéifǎ, "to break the law").

components.note: 女 (woman) — 妹 names a female relative, a younger sister.
未 (wèi) gives a rhyme close to mèi, with a different initial.

example.fact: 妹妹 (mèimei) means younger sister — Chinese distinguishes 姐姐 (jiějie, "older sister") from 妹妹, unlike English "sister."

components.note: 氵 (water) — 浪 names movement on the surface of water, a wave.
良 (liáng) gives a rhyme close to làng, with a different initial and tone.

example.fact: 浪 appears in 海浪 (hǎilàng, "sea wave") and in 浪漫 (làngmàn, "romantic"), a sound loan from the English word "romantic."

etymologyHint: Water 氵 collected in a container 匚

components.note: 氵 (water) forms the flowing liquid part of the picture.
匚 (a container shape) receives the water — together showing water gathering into one place, the source of 汇's meaning 'to converge, to gather.'

example.fact: 汇 depicts water gathering together; today it is also used for financial "remittance," as in 汇款 (huìkuǎn, "to remit money").

components.note: 丿 (a brushstroke mark) — represents writing or a marking on the surface.
巾 (cloth/silk) — early money was silk cloth marked with a value, giving 币 its meaning 'currency.'

example.english: This is a note of RMB.
example.fact: 币 rarely stands alone — it's mostly seen in 人民币 (rénmínbì, "the Chinese currency") and 硬币 (yìngbì, "coin").

components.note: 三 (three lines) — represents stalks or ears of a plant.
丨 (a vertical stroke) — the stem holding them up, together picturing a plant heavy with grain, the source of 丰's meaning 'abundant, bountiful.'

example.english: The fruit here is very abundant.
example.fact: 丰 rarely appears alone in modern Chinese — it's mostly seen in 丰富 (fēngfù, "abundant, rich") and 丰收 (fēngshōu, "a bountiful harvest").

components.note: 艹 (grass/plant) — 蓝 originally named the indigo plant used to make blue dye.
监 (jiān) gives a sound distantly related to lán, having drifted apart over time.

example.fact: 蓝 originally referred to the indigo plant used for dye, before it came to mean the color blue itself.

components.note: 歹 (bad, death) — 殊 originally related to death or being cut off, extended to mean 'set apart, different.'
朱 (zhū) gives a sound close to shū.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè tèshū de qíngkuàng.
example.fact: 殊 almost always appears together with 特 in 特殊 (tèshū, "special"); it is rarely used alone in modern Chinese.

components.note: 犬 (dog) — 献 originally referred to offering a dog in sacrifice, extended to mean 'to offer, present.'
南 (nán) gives a sound distantly related to xiàn, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā wèi guójiā zuòchū le gòngxiàn.
example.english: He made a contribution to the country.
example.fact: 献 commonly appears in 贡献 (gòngxiàn, "contribution") and 献血 (xiànxiě, "to donate blood").

meanings: classifier for tables of guests at a banquet etc

example.english: The book is on the table.
example.fact: 桌子 (zhuōzi) is one of the first words learners meet for basic furniture, along with 椅子 (yǐzi, "chair").

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 啦 is a sentence-final particle, spoken from the mouth.
拉 (lā) is an exact match for the sound of 啦.

example.fact: 啦 is a sentence-final particle that adds emphasis or a lively tone — in sound and feeling it works like a blend of 了 (le) and 啊 (a).

components.note: 瓦 is traditionally read as a picture of a curved, interlocking roof tile, seen in cross-section — the source of its meaning 'tile.'

example.english: The house's roof is covered with tiles.
example.fact: 瓦 names the curved tiles traditionally used to cover Chinese roofs, and today it's also the short form of 瓦特 (wǎtè), the unit "watt."

components.note: 艹 (grass) — 莱 names a weedy plant, goosefoot.
来 (lái) is an exact match for the sound of 莱.

example.fact: 莱 rarely appears alone in modern Chinese — it's mostly seen in place names like 莱州 (Láizhōu), a city in Shandong province.

etymologyHint: To lead 爰 by hand 扌; 爰 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 援 describes reaching out to help someone by hand.
爰 depicts one hand passing something to another, reinforcing the idea of lending aid — together giving 援 its meaning 'to help, to aid.'

example.fact: 援 commonly appears in 支援 (zhīyuán, "to support, back up") and 援助 (yuánzhù, "aid, assistance").

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 译 relates to converting speech or text from one language to another.

example.hanzi: 请把这句话翻译成英文。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhè jù huà fānyì chéng Yīngwén.
example.english: Please translate this sentence into English.
example.fact: 译 almost always appears in 翻译 (fānyì, "to translate") in everyday speech.

etymologyHint: A man 大 grasping something 寸

components.note: 大 (a person, arms spread wide) — depicts someone in the act of grabbing.
寸 (a hand) — grasping at something, together giving 夺 its meaning 'to seize, take by force.'

example.fact: 夺 often appears in 夺得 (duódé, "to win, capture"), especially in sports contexts like winning a championship.

etymologyHint: Liquid 氵 gas 气; 气 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 氵 (water) — 汽 relates to water in its vapor form, steam.
气 (rising wisps) — depicts vapor drifting upward, together giving 汽 its meaning 'steam, gas.'

example.fact: 汽 almost always appears in 汽车 (qìchē, "automobile," literally "steam vehicle") and 汽水 (qìshuǐ, "soda pop").

meanings: to burn; to set on fire
to heat (over a fire); to boil (water, tea etc)

components.note: 火 (fire) — 烧 describes burning or cooking with fire.
尧 (yáo) gives a rhyme close to shāo, with a different initial.

example.fact: 烧 commonly appears in 发烧 (fāshāo, "to have a fever") and 烧烤 (shāokǎo, "barbecue").

meanings: to be at a distance of ... from; to be apart from

components.note: 足 (foot) — 距 relates to the distance covered on foot.
巨 (jù) is an exact match for the sound of 距.

example.hanzi: 学校离我家的距离不远。
example.pinyin: Xuéxiào lí wǒ jiā de jùlí bù yuǎn.
example.english: The distance from school to my home is not far.
example.fact: 距 almost always appears in 距离 (jùlí, "distance") in everyday speech.

etymologyHint: To cut 戈 cloth 衣

components.note: 戈 (a blade) — 裁 involves cutting.
衣 (clothing) — cutting cloth to make or trim clothing, giving 裁 its meaning 'to cut out, to reduce.'

example.fact: 裁 appears in 裁判 (cáipàn, "referee, judge") and 裁缝 (cáifeng, "tailor").

components.note: 亻 (person) — 偏 describes a person's position or attitude leaning to one side.
扁 (biǎn) gives a sound close to piān, sharing the same kind of initial consonant.

example.pinyin: Zhè fú huà guà piān le.
example.fact: 偏 commonly appears in 偏见 (piānjiàn, "prejudice, bias") and describes something tilted or off-center.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — early tallies and charms were carved on strips of bamboo.
付 (fù) gives a sound close to fú, differing only in tone.

example.fact: 符 commonly appears in 符合 (fúhé, "to match, conform to") and 符号 (fúhào, "symbol, sign").

components.note: 力 (strength) — 勇 describes inner strength shown as courage.
甬 (yǒng) is an exact match for the sound of 勇.

example.fact: 勇 almost always appears in 勇敢 (yǒnggǎn, "brave") in everyday speech.

components.note: 角 (horn) — 触 originally described an animal butting or goring with its horns, extended to any physical contact.
虫 (chóng) gives a sound distantly related to chù, having drifted apart over time.

example.fact: 触 commonly appears in 触摸 (chùmō, "to touch") and 接触 (jiēchù, "to come into contact with").

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 课 relates to lessons taught through spoken instruction.
果 (guǒ) gives a sound distantly related to kè, having drifted apart over time.

example.fact: 课 is the basic word for "class, lesson," as in 上课 (shàngkè, "to attend class") and 下课 (xiàkè, "class dismissed").
敬 commonly appears in 尊敬 (zūnjìng, "to respect") and 敬礼 (jìnglǐ, "to salute").

etymologyHint: To shed a tear from your eyes 口 over a person 犬

components.note: 口 (mouth), shown twice here, standing for eyes streaming with tears.
犬 (here a stand-in for a person, not literally 'dog') — a person crying, together giving 哭 its meaning 'to weep, to cry.'

example.fact: 哭 is the everyday verb for "to cry," the opposite of 笑 (xiào, "to laugh").

components.note: 忄 (heart/mind) — 懂 describes understanding something in the mind.
董 (dǒng) is an exact match for the sound of 懂.

example.fact: 懂 is a useful beginner verb, often combined with others like 听懂 (tīngdǒng, "to understand by hearing") and 看懂 (kàndǒng, "to understand by reading").

components.note: 土 (earth) — 墙 names a structure traditionally built from packed earth or brick.
啬 (sè) gives a sound distantly related to qiáng, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Qiáng shàng guàzhe yì zhāng zhàopiàn.
example.english: A photo is hanging on the wall.
example.fact: 墙 is the everyday word for "wall," as in 墙上 (qiáng shàng, "on the wall").

components.note: 龙 (dragon) — historically linked to layered ceremonial robes, extended to mean 'to inherit, pass down' and later 'to raid.'
衣 (yī) gives a rhyme close to xí, with a different initial.

example.pinyin: Táifēng xíjí le zhè zuò chéngshì.
example.fact: 袭 commonly appears in 袭击 (xíjí, "to attack, strike") and 空袭 (kōngxí, "air raid").

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 召 describes calling out to summon someone.
刀 (dāo) gives a rhyme close to zhào, with a different initial.

example.pinyin: Lǎoshī zhàojí le quán bān tóngxué.
example.english: The teacher gathered the whole class.
example.fact: 召 commonly appears in 召集 (zhàojí, "to convene, gather") and 号召 (hàozhào, "to call upon, appeal").

meanings: to punish; to penalize; to fine
etymologyHint: Simplified form of 罰; to punish 刂 the accused 詈

components.note: 罒 (a net) — historically linked to wrongdoing and being caught out.
刂 (a knife/blade) — carrying out punishment, together giving 罚 its meaning 'to punish, penalize.'

example.fact: 罚 commonly appears in 罚款 (fákuǎn, "to fine") and 处罚 (chǔfá, "to punish").

components.note: 亻 (person) — 侠 describes a certain kind of person, a hero.
夹 (jiā) gives a sound close to xiá.

example.fact: 侠 commonly appears in 武侠 (wǔxiá, "martial hero"), the classic genre of Chinese sword-fighting fiction and film.

components.note: 广 (a building/shelter) — 厅 names a large room inside a building, a hall.
丁 (dīng) gives a sound close to tīng.

example.english: We watch TV in the living room.
example.fact: 厅 commonly appears in 客厅 (kètīng, "living room") and 餐厅 (cāntīng, "restaurant, dining hall").

meanings: to bow to; to pay one's respects
to acknowledge sb as one's (master, godfather etc)
etymologyHint: Two hands 手 put together in respect

components.note: 手 (hand), shown twice, side by side — two hands pressed together in a gesture of respect, giving 拜 its meaning 'to bow, to pay respects.'

example.english: I go to visit a friend.
example.fact: 拜 commonly appears in 拜访 (bàifǎng, "to pay a visit") and 拜年 (bàinián, "to give New Year's greetings").

components.note: 工 (work, tool) — 巧 relates to skill in craft or work.
丂 (kǎo) gives a sound close to qiǎo.

example.pinyin: Tā zuò cài de shǒu hěn qiǎo.
example.english: Her hands are skillful at cooking.
example.fact: 巧 commonly appears in 巧克力 (qiǎokèlì, "chocolate," a sound loan) and 凑巧 (còuqiǎo, "coincidentally").

components.note: 亻 (person) — 侧 originally described a person standing to one side.
则 (zé) gives a sound close to cè.

example.english: The school is on the side of the road.
example.fact: 侧 commonly appears in 侧面 (cèmiàn, "side, profile"), the opposite of 正面 (zhèngmiàn, "front").

meanings: Korea from the fall of the Joseon dynasty in 1897
Korea, esp. South Korea 大韓民國|大韩民国

example.fact: 韩 is best known today as part of 韩国 (Hánguó, "Korea").

meanings: to emit; to give off; to send out (or up, forth)

components.note: 目 (eye) — 冒 originally described something extending over or covering, related to a covering over the head.
冃 (mào) is an exact match for the sound of 冒.

example.english: He went to work braving the heavy rain.
example.fact: 冒 commonly appears in 冒险 (màoxiǎn, "to take a risk") and 感冒 (gǎnmào, "to catch a cold").

etymologyHint: A person's 亻 duty 责; 责 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 亻 (person) — 债 concerns something a person owes.
责 (duty, responsibility) — an obligation owed to someone else, together giving 债 its meaning 'debt, loan.'

example.pinyin: Tā qiàn le hěn duō zhài.
example.english: He owes a lot of debt.
example.fact: 债 commonly appears in 欠债 (qiànzhài, "to owe a debt") and 还债 (huánzhài, "to repay a debt").

etymologyHint: Two hands 日, 又 pulling an eye open 罒

components.note: 罒 (an eye) — held open.
又 (a hand) — pulling the eye open wide, together giving 曼 its meaning 'long, extended, graceful.'

example.fact: 曼 is mostly seen in descriptive words like 曼妙 (mànmiào, "graceful") and in place names, like 曼谷 (Màngǔ, "Bangkok").

components.note: 鬲 (an ancient three-legged cauldron) — 融 originally described steam rising from a cooking pot as it heated, i.e. melting or blending.
虫 (chóng) gives a sound distantly related to róng, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Bīng zài yángguāng xià rónghuà le.
example.english: The ice melted in the sunlight.
example.fact: 融 commonly appears in 融化 (rónghuà, "to melt") and 融合 (rónghé, "to blend, fuse").

components.note: 忄 (heart/mind) — 惯 describes a mental pattern, a habit.
贯 (guàn) is an exact match for the sound of 惯.

example.english: I'm used to getting up early.
example.fact: 惯 almost always appears in 习惯 (xíguàn, "habit, to be used to") in everyday speech.

etymologyHint: Children 子 living and eating 口 in the house 亠

components.note: 亠 (a roof) — the top of a house.
口 (a mouth) — eating and enjoying inside it.
子 (a child) — together showing a family living and eating well under one roof, giving 享 its meaning 'to enjoy.'

example.fact: 享 commonly appears in 享受 (xiǎngshòu, "to enjoy") and 分享 (fēnxiǎng, "to share").

meanings: to put on or wear (glasses, hat, gloves etc)

example.english: She is wearing a pair of glasses.
example.fact: 戴 is used for wearing things on the head or extremities — glasses, hats, watches — while 穿 is used for clothes.

etymologyHint: A child standing 立 in the village 里

components.note: 立 (standing) — a small figure standing upright.
里 here representing a village or settlement, together giving 童 its meaning 'child.'

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yì běn értóng dúwù.
example.fact: 童 commonly appears in 儿童 (értóng, "children") and 童年 (tóngnián, "childhood").

components.note: 犭 (dog/animal) — historically linked to a wary, hesitant animal, extended to mean 'as if, similar to.'
尤 (yóu) is an exact match for the sound of 犹.

example.english: He hesitated for a long time.
example.fact: 犹 commonly appears in 犹豫 (yóuyù, "to hesitate") and 犹如 (yóurú, "just as, like").

etymologyHint: Two feet 北 climbing a beanstalk 禾

components.note: 北 here representing two feet or footprints, one behind the other.
禾 (a stalk of grain), here standing in for a tree or ladder — together depicting someone climbing up, giving 乘 its meaning 'to ride, to get onto.'

example.english: I take the bus to work every day.
example.fact: 乘 is a somewhat formal word for "to ride, take (transportation)," as in 乘车 (chéngchē, "to take a vehicle") and 乘客 (chéngkè, "passenger").

meanings: to hang; to suspend (from a hook etc)

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 挂 describes hanging something up using the hand.
圭 (guī) gives a sound close to guà, sharing the initial g-.

example.pinyin: Qiáng shàng guàzhe yì fú huà.
example.english: A painting is hanging on the wall.
example.fact: 挂 is the everyday verb for "to hang," as in 挂衣服 (guà yīfu, "to hang up clothes") and 挂电话 (guà diànhuà, "to hang up the phone").

meanings: (bound form) to encourage; to commend; to praise
to award; to give as a reward

components.note: 大 (big) — 奖 describes something given as a big reward.
丬 (qiáng) gives a sound close to jiǎng.

example.pinyin: Tā dé le dì-yī míng de jiǎng.
example.fact: 奖 commonly appears in 奖品 (jiǎngpǐn, "prize") and 得奖 (déjiǎng, "to win an award").

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 绍 originally related to connecting threads, extended to mean 'to continue, carry on' and 'to introduce.'
召 (zhào) gives a sound close to shào.

example.hanzi: 请让我介绍一下我自己。
example.pinyin: Qǐng ràng wǒ jièshào yíxià wǒ zìjǐ.
example.fact: 绍 almost always appears in 介绍 (jièshào, "to introduce") in everyday speech.

etymologyHint: Sunlight 日 and children 子 in a building 厂

components.note: 厂 (a building/shelter) — forms the enclosing shape.
日 (sunlight) — light streaming inside.
子 (children) — together suggesting a household full of light and family, giving 厚 its meaning 'thick, substantial, generous.'

example.fact: 厚 is the basic word for "thick," the opposite of 薄 (báo, "thin").

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 纵 originally described letting a thread run loose, extended to mean 'to indulge, release.'
从 (cóng) gives a sound close to zòng.

example.english: Parents shouldn't indulge their children too much.
example.fact: 纵 commonly appears in 纵容 (zòngróng, "to indulge, condone") and 放纵 (fàngzòng, "to be unrestrained").

components.note: 阝 (mound, related to walls and terrain) — 障 describes something that blocks a path, like a wall.
章 (zhāng) gives a sound close to zhàng, differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè hěn dà de zhàng'ài.
example.english: This is a very big obstacle.
example.fact: 障 almost always appears in 障碍 (zhàng'ài, "obstacle, barrier") in everyday speech.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — 讯 relates to asking questions and gathering information through words.
卂 (xùn) is an exact match for the sound of 讯.

example.pinyin: Qǐng kàn jīntiān de xīnwén zīxùn.
example.fact: 讯 commonly appears in 资讯 (zīxùn, "information") and 通讯 (tōngxùn, "communication").

meanings: (literary) to wade across a body of water
etymologyHint: To wade 步 through a stream 氵

components.note: 氵 (water/stream) — the water being crossed.
步 (to step, walk) — feet moving through it, together giving 涉 its meaning 'to wade across' and, more broadly, 'to be involved in.'

example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì shèjí hěn duō rén.
example.fact: 涉 commonly appears in 涉及 (shèjí, "to involve, relate to"), describing a topic touching on many things.

components.note: 切 (to cut) — 彻 describes something carried through completely, as if cutting all the way through.
彳 (chì) gives a sound close to chè.

example.hanzi: 他把房间彻底打扫了一遍。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ fángjiān chèdǐ dǎsǎo le yí biàn.
example.fact: 彻 almost always appears in 彻底 (chèdǐ, "thorough, complete") in everyday speech.

components.note: 刂 (knife) — 刊 originally meant to carve or engrave onto wood blocks for printing.
干 (gān) gives a sound close to kān, sharing the same rhyme.

example.english: This magazine is a monthly publication.
example.fact: 刊 commonly appears in 月刊 (yuèkān, "monthly publication") and 刊登 (kāndēng, "to publish, print").

meanings: measure of length, ten Chinese feet (3.3 m)

example.fact: 丈 is best known today as part of 丈夫 (zhàngfu, "husband"); its original meaning was a unit of length, about 3.3 meters.

etymologyHint: A violent 暴 flame 火; 暴 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 火 (fire) — flame at the heart of the picture.
暴 (violent, sudden) — a burst of intense fire, together giving 爆 its meaning 'to explode, burst.'

example.fact: 爆 commonly appears in 爆炸 (bàozhà, "to explode") and 爆米花 (bàomǐhuā, "popcorn").

etymologyHint: Simplified form of 烏; a crow; compare 鸟

components.note: 乌 (a simplified form of 烏) depicts a crow in silhouette — traditionally said to lack the dot for an eye that 鸟 ('bird') has, since a crow's dark eye disappears into its black feathers.

example.pinyin: Tiān shàng fēi lái yì zhī wūyā.
example.english: A crow flew over in the sky.
example.fact: 乌 almost always appears in 乌鸦 (wūyā, "crow") and 乌云 (wūyún, "dark clouds"), both drawing on its sense of "black, dark."

etymologyHint: A person walking over 彳 with food in hand 殳

components.note: 彳 (to walk) — a person moving, sent somewhere to work.
殳 (a tool held in the hand) — carrying out labor, together giving 役 its meaning 'service, forced labor.'

example.english: He is doing his military service.
example.fact: 役 commonly appears in 兵役 (bīngyì, "military service") and 服役 (fúyì, "to serve (in the military or a role)").

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 描 describes tracing or drawing something by hand.
苗 (miáo) is an exact match for the sound of 描.

example.pinyin: Tā zài miáo yì zhāng huà.
example.fact: 描 commonly appears in 描写 (miáoxiě, "to describe") and 描述 (miáoshù, "to depict, describe").

components.note: 氵 (water) — 洗 describes cleaning something with water.
先 (xiān) shares the initial x- with xǐ, though the rhyme has drifted.

example.english: I take a shower every day.
example.fact: 洗 is a basic everyday verb, seen in 洗澡 (xǐzǎo, "to bathe"), 洗手 (xǐshǒu, "to wash hands"), and 洗衣服 (xǐ yīfu, "to do laundry").

meanings: used in 瑪瑙|玛瑙[ma3 nao3]

components.note: 王 (jade, written as the radical for 玉) — 玛 names a type of precious stone, agate.
马 (mǎ) is an exact match for the sound of 玛.

example.english: This is a piece of agate.
example.fact: 玛 almost always appears in 玛瑙 (mǎnǎo, "agate") or in transliterated foreign names, like 玛丽 (Mǎlì, "Mary").

components.note: 心 (heart/mind) — 患 describes a burden weighing on the mind, worry or suffering.
串 (chuàn) gives a rhyme close to huàn, with a different initial.

example.english: He suffered from a serious illness.
example.fact: 患 commonly appears in 患者 (huànzhě, "patient") and 患病 (huànbìng, "to fall ill").

components.note: 女 (woman) — 妙 originally described a young woman's delicate charm, extended to mean 'wonderful, clever.'
少 (shǎo) gives a sound distantly related to miào, having drifted apart over time.

example.fact: 妙 commonly appears in 奇妙 (qímiào, "marvelous, curious") and 妙极了 (miào jí le, "wonderful!").

components.note: 钅 (metal) — early mirrors were made of polished bronze.
竟 (jìng) is an exact match for the sound of 镜.

example.english: She is looking in the mirror.
example.fact: 镜 commonly appears in 镜子 (jìngzi, "mirror") and 眼镜 (yǎnjìng, "glasses").

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 唱 describes singing, an action made with the mouth.
昌 (chāng) gives a sound close to chàng, differing only in tone.

example.fact: 唱 is the everyday verb for "to sing," as in 唱歌 (chànggē, "to sing a song") and 唱片 (chàngpiàn, "record, album").

components.note: 火 (fire) — 烦 describes a burning, irritated feeling.
页 (yè) gives a sound distantly related to fán, having drifted apart over time.

example.fact: 烦 almost always appears in 麻烦 (máfan, "troublesome, to bother") and 烦恼 (fánnǎo, "worry, annoyance").

meanings: to write brief comments on a document
inscribed bamboo stick (variant of 籤|签[qian1])

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — early signature tallies and slips were made of bamboo.
佥 (qiān) is an exact match for the sound of 签.

example.fact: 签 commonly appears in 签名 (qiānmíng, "to sign one's name") and 签证 (qiānzhèng, "visa").

components.note: 亻 (person) — 仙 describes a special kind of person, an immortal being.
山 (shān) gives a sound close to xiān.

example.english: There are immortals in this story.
example.fact: 仙 commonly appears in 神仙 (shénxiān, "immortal, deity") from Chinese mythology and folk tales.

components.note: 彳 (to walk, step) — 彼 originally related to distance, extended to mean 'that, the other.'
皮 (pí) gives a sound close to bǐ.

example.fact: 彼 mostly appears in the set phrase 彼此 (bǐcǐ, "each other, one another").

etymologyHint: Two arrows 丨 pulled across a bow

components.note: 弓 (a bow) — the curved frame.
丨 (a straight line), shown twice — arrows or a bowstring pulled tight across it; the character is mostly used today in transliteration.

example.fact: 弗 is rarely used for its own meaning today ("not") — it mostly appears in transliterated foreign names, like 弗兰克 (Fúlánkè, "Frank").

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — 症 names a symptom or disease.
正 (zhèng) is an exact match for the sound of 症.

example.pinyin: Yīshēng zài jiǎnchá tā de zhèngzhuàng.
example.english: The doctor is examining his symptoms.
example.fact: 症 commonly appears in 症状 (zhèngzhuàng, "symptom") and in words for specific conditions, like 癌症 (áizhèng, "cancer").

components.note: 亻 (person) — 仿 describes one person copying another.
方 (fāng) gives a sound close to fǎng, differing only in tone.

example.fact: 仿 commonly appears in 模仿 (mófǎng, "to imitate, mimic") and 仿佛 (fǎngfú, "as if, seemingly").

components.note: 亻 (person) — 倾 describes a person or thing tilting or leaning.
顷 (qǐng) gives a sound close to qīng, differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Zhè zuò tǎ zài mànmàn qīngxié.
example.fact: 倾 commonly appears in 倾斜 (qīngxié, "to tilt, slant") and 倾向 (qīngxiàng, "tendency, inclination").

components.note: 片 (a thin slice/board) — 牌 names a flat board or sign, like a nameplate.
卑 (bēi) gives a sound close to pái.

example.english: A sign is hanging by the door.
example.fact: 牌 commonly appears in 牌子 (páizi, "sign, brand") and 打牌 (dǎpái, "to play cards").

etymologyHint: A place 阝 with a pit 臽; 臽 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 阝 (a mound, related to terrain) — the ground where something happens.
臽 (a pit) — a hole in the ground, together giving 陷 its meaning 'to sink, to fall into a trap.'

example.pinyin: Chēlún xiàn jìn le ní lǐ.
example.english: The wheel got stuck in the mud.
example.fact: 陷 commonly appears in 陷入 (xiànrù, "to fall/sink into") and 陷阱 (xiànjǐng, "trap, pitfall").

etymologyHint: Simplified form of 烏, a bird

components.note: 鸟 (a simplified form of 鳥) is a simple picture of a bird in profile — its head, wing, and tail are still visible in the strokes.

example.pinyin: Shù shàng yǒu yì zhī xiǎo niǎo.
example.english: There is a little bird in the tree.
example.fact: 鸟 is the general word for "bird"; its measure word is 只 (zhī), as in 一只鸟 (yì zhī niǎo, "a bird").

etymologyHint: The thunderous sound of a pair 双 of carts 车

components.note: 车 (a cart) — a rumbling vehicle.
双 (a pair) — two such carts together, their combined noise giving 轰 its meaning 'rumble, boom, to bombard.'

example.pinyin: Wàimiàn chuánlái hōng de yì shēng.
example.english: A boom sound came from outside.
example.fact: 轰 imitates a loud rumbling sound, and commonly appears in 轰炸 (hōngzhà, "to bomb") and 轰动 (hōngdòng, "to cause a sensation").

components.note: 口 (mouth) — 咱 is a spoken pronoun, used in speech.
自 (zì) shares the initial z- with zán, though the rhyme has drifted.

example.fact: 咱 is a casual, colloquial way to say "we/us," often heard in northern Chinese speech as 咱们 (zánmen).

components.note: 艹 (plant) — 菜 names something grown, a vegetable.
采 (cǎi) gives a sound close to cài, differing only in tone.

example.fact: 菜 means both "vegetable" and, more broadly, any prepared "dish," as in 中国菜 (Zhōngguó cài, "Chinese cuisine").

etymologyHint: A door 门 blocked by bars 才

components.note: 门 (a door) — the frame of a doorway.
才 here representing a bar or beam laid across it, together giving 闭 its meaning 'to close, shut, block up.'

example.fact: 闭 commonly appears in 闭上 (bì shàng, "to close (eyes, mouth)") and 关闭 (guānbì, "to shut down, close").

etymologyHint: A man 大 working on the farm 田

components.note: 大 (a person) — arms spread, exerting effort.
田 (a field) — working hard on the land, together giving 奋 its meaning 'to strive, exert oneself.'

example.fact: 奋 commonly appears in 奋斗 (fèndòu, "to strive, struggle") and 兴奋 (xīngfèn, "excited").

etymologyHint: A great 大 celebration in a house 广

components.note: 广 (a building/shelter) — the setting of the celebration.
大 (great, big) — a grand event held inside, together giving 庆 its meaning 'to celebrate.'

example.fact: 庆 almost always appears in 庆祝 (qìngzhù, "to celebrate") in everyday speech.
撤 commonly appears in 撤退 (chètuì, "to retreat") and 撤销 (chèxiāo, "to cancel, revoke").

etymologyHint: Water 氵 from the eyes 目

components.note: 氵 (water) — the liquid falling.
目 (eye) — together showing water falling from the eyes, giving 泪 its meaning 'tears.'

example.fact: 泪 almost always appears in 眼泪 (yǎnlèi, "tears") in everyday speech.

components.note: 艹 (plant) — 茶 names a plant, the tea plant, and the drink made from it.

example.fact: 茶 gave English the word "tea," one of many Chinese loanwords that traveled the world along trade routes.

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — 疾 names a disease or ailment.
矢 (shǐ) gives a sound distantly related to jí, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Tā dé le yì zhǒng jíbìng.
example.fact: 疾 almost always appears in 疾病 (jíbìng, "disease, illness") in everyday speech.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 缘 originally described the hemmed edge of cloth, extended to mean 'connection, fate.'
彖 (tuàn) gives a sound distantly related to yuán, having drifted apart over time.

example.english: This is really a kind of fate.
example.fact: 缘 commonly appears in 缘分 (yuánfèn, "fate, destiny that brings people together") and 因缘 (yīnyuán, "karma, causal connection").

etymologyHint: To sow seeds 番 by hand 扌; 番 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 扌 (hand) — the hand doing the sowing.
番 (a field marked out into plots) — seeds scattered by hand across it, giving 播 its meaning 'to sow, to spread, to broadcast.'

example.fact: 播 commonly appears in 播放 (bōfàng, "to play, broadcast") and 广播 (guǎngbō, "radio broadcast").

components.note: 月 (moon) — 朗 describes the moon's bright, clear light.
良 (liáng) gives a rhyme close to lǎng, with a different initial.

example.english: The weather is very clear tonight.
example.fact: 朗 commonly appears in 晴朗 (qínglǎng, "sunny and clear") and 朗读 (lǎngdú, "to read aloud").

components.note: 木 (tree) — 杜 names a kind of tree, the birchleaf pear.
土 (tǔ) gives a sound close to dù.

example.fact: 杜 is common as a surname; it also appears in 杜绝 (dùjué, "to put an end to, prevent completely").

components.note: 女 (woman) — 奶 relates to a woman nursing, and to milk.
乃 (nǎi) is an exact match for the sound of 奶.

example.fact: 奶 commonly appears in 牛奶 (niúnǎi, "cow's milk") and 奶奶 (nǎinai, "grandmother, paternal").

meanings: the last month of a season
etymologyHint: The time for planting seeds 子 of grain 禾

components.note: 禾 (a grain stalk) — a crop ready for harvest.
子 here representing a seed, together giving 季 its meaning 'season,' the time for planting and harvest.

example.hanzi: 春天是我最喜欢的季节。
example.pinyin: Chūntiān shì wǒ zuì xǐhuan de jìjié.
example.fact: 季 almost always appears in 季节 (jìjié, "season") in everyday speech.

etymologyHint: A red pellet 丶 from a mine 井

components.note: 丹 depicts a pellet of red cinnabar mineral, dug from a mine — the source of its meaning 'cinnabar, red, pellet.'

example.pinyin: Mǔdan shì yì zhǒng hěn měi de huā.
example.english: The peony is a very beautiful flower.
example.fact: 丹 commonly appears in 牡丹 (mǔdan, "peony," a flower prized in Chinese culture) and as part of names, since it also means "red."

components.note: 犭 (dog/animal) — 狗 names an animal, the dog.
句 (jù) gives a sound distantly related to gǒu, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǒu yì zhī gǒu.
example.fact: 狗 is one of the first animal words learners meet, with measure word 只 (zhī), as in 一只狗 (yì zhī gǒu, "a dog").

etymologyHint: A furry 毛 tail behind a body 尸

components.note: 尸 (a body) — the body of an animal.
毛 (fur/hair) — trailing behind it, together giving 尾 its meaning 'tail.'

example.english: The puppy is wagging its tail.
example.fact: 尾 almost always appears in 尾巴 (wěibā, "tail") in everyday speech.

components.note: 义 (yì) gives a sound close to yí, differing only in tone.

example.english: The wedding ceremony is very special.
example.fact: 仪 commonly appears in 仪式 (yíshì, "ceremony, ritual") and 礼仪 (lǐyí, "etiquette, protocol").

components.note: 亻 (person) — 偷 describes a person's action, stealing.
俞 (yú) gives a sound distantly related to tōu, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Yǒurén tōu le wǒ de qiánbāo.
example.fact: 偷 is the everyday verb for "to steal," as in 小偷 (xiǎotōu, "thief").

etymologyHint: A man 大 running through a field of grass 卉

components.note: 大 (a person, arms and legs spread) — running with full strides.
卉 here representing a field of grass or plants, together giving 奔 its meaning 'to run fast, to rush.'

example.english: He rushed toward the finish line.
example.fact: 奔 commonly appears in 奔跑 (bēnpǎo, "to run") and 奔波 (bēnbō, "to rush about, toil").

components.note: 王 (jade, written as the radical for 玉) — 珠 names a round gem or bead.
朱 (zhū) is an exact match for the sound of 珠.

example.pinyin: Tā dàizhe yì tiáo zhūzi xiàngliàn.
example.english: She is wearing a beaded necklace.
example.fact: 珠 commonly appears in 珍珠 (zhēnzhū, "pearl") and 珠子 (zhūzi, "bead").

components.note: 中 (zhōng) gives a sound close to chóng, sharing the same rhyme.

example.pinyin: Shù shàng yǒu yì zhī chóngzi.
example.english: There is a bug on the tree.
example.fact: 虫 is the general word for insects and small crawling creatures, as in 虫子 (chóngzi, "bug, insect").

meanings: to be stationed (of troops, diplomats etc)

components.note: 马 (horse) — 驻 originally described a horse stopping and standing still, extended to mean 'to be stationed.'
主 (zhǔ) gives a sound close to zhù, differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Zhèlǐ zhùzhá zhe yì zhī jūnduì.
example.fact: 驻 commonly appears in 驻扎 (zhùzhá, "to be stationed") and in words for diplomats, like 驻华大使 (zhùhuá dàshǐ, "ambassador to China").

etymologyHint: The mouth 乚 of a crying baby 子

components.note: 子 (a baby) — a small child.
乚 (a hook shape) — here representing an open, crying mouth, together giving 孔 its meaning 'hole, opening.'

example.pinyin: Zhè kuài mùbǎn shàng yǒu yí gè kǒng.
example.english: There is a hole in this wooden board.
example.fact: 孔 is also a very famous surname — 孔子 (Kǒngzǐ) is Confucius, China's most influential philosopher.

etymologyHint: A memorial service 且 held in a house 宀

components.note: 宀 (a roof) — the shelter of a house.
且 here representing an altar or memorial tablet, together suggesting a fitting, proper ceremony held at home, giving 宜 its meaning 'suitable, fitting.'

example.english: The weather here is very pleasant.
example.fact: 宜 commonly appears in 便宜 (piányi, "cheap, inexpensive") and 适宜 (shìyí, "suitable").

components.note: 艹 (plant) — 艾 names a plant, mugwort.
乂 (yì) gives a sound distantly related to ài, having drifted apart over time.

example.english: During the Dragon Boat Festival, people hang mugwort.
example.fact: 艾 names mugwort (艾草, àicǎo), a plant traditionally hung on doors during the Dragon Boat Festival to ward off illness.

components.note: 木 (tree/wood) — 桥 names a structure traditionally built of wood.
乔 (qiáo) is an exact match for the sound of 桥.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen zǒuguò le yí zuò qiáo.
example.fact: 桥 is the basic word for "bridge," with measure word 座 (zuò), as in 一座桥 (yí zuò qiáo, "a bridge").

components.note: 氵 (water) — 淡 describes something diluted or watery, weak in taste.
炎 (yán) gives a sound distantly related to dàn, having drifted apart over time.

example.fact: 淡 describes something weak or bland in taste, the opposite of 浓 (nóng, "strong, concentrated").

meanings: area surrounding the bullseye of a target

components.note: 羽 (feather) — 翼 names a wing, covered in feathers.
異 (yì) is an exact match for the sound of 翼.

example.english: The airplane's wing is very long.
example.fact: 翼 commonly appears in 机翼 (jīyì, "airplane wing") and 左翼/右翼 (zuǒyì/yòuyì, "left/right wing," also used politically).

components.note: 忄 (heart/mind) — 恨 describes a strong feeling in the heart, hatred.
艮 (gèn) gives a sound close to hèn.

example.fact: 恨 is the basic verb for "to hate," often contrasted with 爱 (ài, "to love").

components.note: 糸 (silk/thread) — 繁 originally described many intertwined threads, extended to mean 'complicated, numerous.'
敏 (mǐn) gives a sound distantly related to fán, having drifted apart over time.

example.fact: 繁 commonly appears in 繁忙 (fánmáng, "busy") and 繁体字 (fántǐzì, "traditional Chinese characters").
寒 commonly appears in 寒冷 (hánlěng, "cold") and 寒假 (hánjià, "winter vacation").

components.note: 亻 (person) — 伴 describes a person accompanying another.
半 (bàn) is an exact match for the sound of 伴.

example.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ zuì hǎo de huǒbàn.
example.fact: 伴 commonly appears in 伙伴 (huǒbàn, "partner, companion") and 陪伴 (péibàn, "to accompany").

etymologyHint: A mouth 口 exhaling 又

components.note: 口 (mouth) — where the breath is released.
又 here representing a puff of air let out, together giving 叹 its meaning 'to sigh, exclaim.'

example.pinyin: Tā tàn le yì kǒu qì.
example.fact: 叹 commonly appears in 叹气 (tànqì, "to sigh") and 感叹 (gǎntàn, "to exclaim, sigh with feeling").

etymologyHint: The sun 日 rising over the horizon 一

components.note: 日 (the sun) — rising above.
一 (a horizontal line) — the horizon, together giving 旦 its meaning 'dawn, daybreak.'

example.fact: 旦 commonly appears in 元旦 (Yuándàn, "New Year's Day") and 一旦 (yídàn, "once, as soon as").

components.note: 心 (heart/mind) — 愈 relates to the mind or body recovering.
俞 (yú) gives a sound close to yù, differing only in tone.

example.english: The weather is getting colder and colder.
example.fact: 愈 commonly appears in the pattern 愈来愈 (yùláiyù, "more and more") and in 愈合 (yùhé, "to heal").

components.note: 氵 (water) — 潮 names the rise and fall of the sea, the tide.
朝 (cháo) is an exact match for the sound of 潮.

example.english: Now is the time of the rising tide.
example.fact: 潮 commonly appears in 潮水 (cháoshuǐ, "tide") and 潮湿 (cháoshī, "damp, humid").

components.note: 米 (rice/grain) — 粮 names food, especially grain.
良 (liáng) is an exact match for the sound of 粮.

example.fact: 粮 almost always appears in 粮食 (liángshi, "food grain, provisions") in everyday speech.

components.note: 纟 (thread) — 缩 describes thread pulling tight and shrinking.
宿 (sù) gives a sound close to suō.

example.hanzi: 这件毛衣洗了以后缩水了。
example.pinyin: Zhè jiàn máoyī xǐ le yǐhòu suōshuǐ le.
example.english: This sweater shrank after being washed.
example.fact: 缩 commonly appears in 缩小 (suōxiǎo, "to shrink, reduce") and 缩短 (suōduǎn, "to shorten").

etymologyHint: Stuck in a net 罒, unable to leave 去

components.note: 罒 (a net) — something trapped inside it.
去 (to leave, go) — unable to get away, together giving 罢 its meaning 'to stop, cease.'

example.english: The workers decided to go on strike.
example.fact: 罢 commonly appears in 罢工 (bàgōng, "to strike, walk off the job") and 罢休 (bàxiū, "to give up, stop").

etymologyHint: People standing side-by-side 乑, hand-to-ear 取

components.note: 取 (a hand at an ear) — gathering information or people.
乑 (people standing side by side) — together giving 聚 its meaning 'to assemble, gather.'

example.fact: 聚 commonly appears in 聚会 (jùhuì, "gathering, party") and 聚集 (jùjí, "to gather, assemble").

meanings: footpath; path; track; (fig.) a way; a means

components.note: 彳 (to walk, step) — 径 names a small path for walking.
工 (gōng) gives a sound distantly related to jìng, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Gōngyuán lǐ yǒu yì tiáo xiǎojìng.
example.english: There is a small path in the park.
example.fact: 径 commonly appears in 小径 (xiǎojìng, "small path") and 直径 (zhíjìng, "diameter").

components.note: 忄 (heart/mind) — 恰 describes something that fits exactly as intended.
合 (hé) gives a sound distantly related to qià, having drifted apart over time.

example.english: You came at just the right time.
example.fact: 恰 commonly appears in 恰好 (qiàhǎo, "exactly, just right") and 恰巧 (qiàqiǎo, "by coincidence").

meanings: a load carried on the shoulders
to carry on a shoulder pole

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 挑 describes an action done with the hand, picking or carrying.
兆 (zhào) gives a sound distantly related to tiāo, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Wǒ yào tiāo yí jiàn lǐwù.
example.english: I want to pick out a gift.
example.fact: 挑 commonly appears in 挑选 (tiāoxuǎn, "to select, choose") and 挑食 (tiāoshí, "to be picky about food").

components.note: 衣 (clothing) — 袋 names something made of cloth or similar material, a bag.
代 (dài) is an exact match for the sound of 袋.

example.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ yí gè dàizi.
example.fact: 袋 commonly appears in 袋子 (dàizi, "bag") and 口袋 (kǒudài, "pocket").

etymologyHint: The remains of a fire 火; 火 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 灰 depicts the leftover ash of a fire 火 below, mixed with dust — the source of its meaning 'ash, gray.'

example.pinyin: Qiáng shàng yǒu yì céng huī.
example.english: There is a layer of dust on the wall.
example.fact: 灰 means both "ash" and the color "gray," as in 灰色 (huīsè, "gray").

meanings: to catch; to seize; to capture

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 捕 describes catching something with the hands.
甫 (fǔ) gives a sound close to bǔ, sharing the same kind of initial consonant.

example.fact: 捕 commonly appears in 逮捕 (dàibǔ, "to arrest") and 捕鱼 (bǔyú, "to catch fish").

components.note: 彳 (to walk, step) — 徐 describes a slow, calm way of moving.
余 (yú) gives a sound close to xú, sharing the same rhyme.

example.fact: 徐 is common as a surname; on its own it also means "slowly, calmly," as in 徐徐 (xúxú, "slowly").

components.note: 王 (jade, written as the radical for 玉) — 珍 names something precious, like a valuable jewel.
彡 (shān) gives a sound distantly related to zhēn, having drifted apart over time.

example.pinyin: Zhè shì yí jiàn zhēnguì de lǐwù.
example.fact: 珍 commonly appears in 珍贵 (zhēnguì, "precious, valuable") and 珍惜 (zhēnxī, "to cherish, treasure").

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — 幕 names a large piece of cloth, a curtain or screen.
莫 (mò) gives a sound close to mù, sharing the same rhyme.

example.fact: 幕 commonly appears in 屏幕 (píngmù, "screen") and 开幕 (kāimù, "to open, as of a curtain or ceremony").

components.note: 日 (sun) — 映 describes light reflecting or shining.
央 (yāng) shares the initial y- with yìng, though the rhyme has drifted.

example.english: Moonlight is reflected on the water's surface.
example.fact: 映 commonly appears in 反映 (fǎnyìng, "to reflect, report") and 放映 (fàngyìng, "to project, screen a film").

components.note: 衣 (cloth) — 裂 describes cloth tearing apart.
列 (liè) is an exact match for the sound of 裂.

example.pinyin: Bēizi liè le yì tiáo fèng.
example.fact: 裂 commonly appears in 裂开 (lièkāi, "to split open") and 分裂 (fēnliè, "to split, divide").

meanings: Mt Tai 泰山[Tai4 Shan1] in Shandong
etymologyHint: Water 氺 contained by a dam

components.note: 泰 depicts a great volume of water 氺 being controlled or channeled from above — mastery over something so large came to suggest greatness, giving 泰 its meaning 'great, exalted.'

example.pinyin: Tài Shān shì Zhōngguó de míngshān.
example.english: Mount Tai is a famous mountain in China.
example.fact: 泰 is best known today in 泰山 (Tài Shān, "Mount Tai," one of China's most sacred mountains) and 泰国 (Tàiguó, "Thailand").

components.note: 阝 (mound, related to walls) — 隔 describes something separated by a barrier.
鬲 (gé) is an exact match for the sound of 隔.

example.hanzi: 我们隔壁住着一个老人。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen gébì zhùzhe yí gè lǎorén.
example.english: An elderly person lives next door to us.
example.fact: 隔 commonly appears in 隔壁 (gébì, "next door") and 间隔 (jiàngé, "interval, gap").

etymologyHint: A door 户 being opened 口

components.note: 户 (a door) — the panel of a door.
口 (an opening) — the door swinging open, together giving 启 its meaning 'to open, to begin.'

example.english: The trip is about to begin.
example.fact: 启 commonly appears in 启程 (qǐchéng, "to set out on a journey") and 开启 (kāiqǐ, "to open, start up").

etymologyHint: A point, small 小 over big 大

components.note: 小 (small) — a narrow point at the top.
大 (big) — a wider base below, together giving 尖 its meaning 'sharp, pointed.'

example.fact: 尖 describes anything that comes to a point, as in 笔尖 (bǐjiān, "pen tip") and 尖叫 (jiānjiào, "to scream, shriek").

components.note: 心 (heart/mind) — 忠 describes a heart that stays true, loyalty.
中 (zhōng) is an exact match for the sound of 忠.

example.english: He is very loyal to his friends.
example.fact: 忠 commonly appears in 忠诚 (zhōngchéng, "loyal, faithful") and 忠实 (zhōngshí, "faithful, devoted").

etymologyHint: Simplified form of 纍; growing silk 糸 in the fields 畾; 畾 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 田 (fields), standing in for 畾 — plots of land.
糸 (silk/thread) — bundles produced across the fields, together giving 累 its meaning 'tired, to accumulate.'

example.fact: 累 is one of the most common adjectives learners need for describing feeling tired after a long day.

components.note: 炎 shows 火 (fire) twice, stacked — flames rising high, giving 炎 its meaning 'flame, blazing, inflammation.'

example.fact: 炎 commonly appears in 炎热 (yánrè, "scorching hot") and in medical terms for inflammation, like 发炎 (fāyán, "to become inflamed").

components.note: 日 (sun, related to time) — 暂 describes a short span of time.
斩 (zhǎn) gives a sound close to zàn.

example.fact: 暂 commonly appears in 暂时 (zànshí, "temporary, for the moment") and 暂停 (zàntíng, "to pause, suspend").

components.note: 亻 (person) — 估 describes a person making a judgment or guess.
古 (gǔ) gives a sound close to gū, differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Wǒ gūjì tā míngtiān huì lái.
example.english: I estimate he will come tomorrow.
example.fact: 估 almost always appears in 估计 (gūjì, "to estimate, guess") in everyday speech.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 泛 describes something floating or spreading on water.
乏 (fá) gives a sound close to fàn.

example.hanzi: 这个词有很广泛的意思。
example.pinyin: Zhège cí yǒu hěn guǎngfàn de yìsi.
example.english: This word has a very broad meaning.
example.fact: 泛 commonly appears in 广泛 (guǎngfàn, "extensive, widespread") and 泛滥 (fànlàn, "to flood, overflow").

components.note: 芒 (the tip of a plant, an awn) — 荒 relates to overgrown, uncultivated land.
川 (chuān) gives a sound distantly related to huāng, having drifted apart over time.

example.english: This piece of land is wasteland.
example.fact: 荒 commonly appears in 荒地 (huāngdì, "wasteland") and 荒岛 (huāngdǎo, "deserted island").

components.note: 亻 (person) — 偿 describes a person repaying something owed.
尝 (cháng) is an exact match for the sound of 偿.

example.english: He must compensate for the loss.
example.fact: 偿 commonly appears in 赔偿 (péicháng, "to compensate") and 补偿 (bǔcháng, "to make up for, compensate").

components.note: 木 (tree/wood) — 横 originally described a wooden crossbar or beam laid horizontally.
黄 (huáng) shares the initial h- with héng, though the rhyme has drifted.

example.fact: 横 describes anything lying flat and crosswise, as in 横线 (héngxiàn, "horizontal line") — the opposite of 竖 (shù, "vertical").

components.note: 扌 (hand) — 拒 describes pushing something away with the hand, refusing.
巨 (jù) is an exact match for the sound of 拒.

example.pinyin: Tā jùjué le wǒ de qǐngqiú.
example.fact: 拒 almost always appears in 拒绝 (jùjué, "to refuse, reject") in everyday speech.

components.note: 王 (jade, written as the radical for 玉) — 瑞 describes a jade tablet used as a token of good fortune.
耑 (duān) gives a sound distantly related to ruì, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 瑞士是一个美丽的国家。
example.pinyin: Ruìshì shì yí gè měilì de guójiā.
example.fact: 瑞 originally meant "auspicious, lucky," and today it's also used to transliterate foreign names, as in 瑞士 (Ruìshì, "Switzerland") and 瑞典 (Ruìdiǎn, "Sweden").

components.note: 忄 (heart/mind) — 忆 describes holding something in the mind, memory.
乙 (yǐ) gives a sound close to yì, differing only in tone.

example.pinyin: Zhè ràng wǒ huíyì qǐ xiǎoshíhou.
example.english: This reminds me of my childhood.
example.fact: 忆 almost always appears in 回忆 (huíyì, "to recall, memory") and 记忆 (jìyì, "memory").

components.note: 子 (child) — 孤 originally described a child without a parent, an orphan.
瓜 (guā) gives a sound close to gū, sharing the same initial.

example.fact: 孤 commonly appears in 孤独 (gūdú, "lonely, solitary") and 孤儿 (gū'ér, "orphan").

components.note: 自 (originally a picture of a nose) — 鼻 names the nose.
畀 (bì) gives a sound close to bí, differing only in tone.

example.fact: 鼻 is the basic word for "nose," as in 鼻子 (bízi); interestingly, 自 ("self") was originally a picture of a nose, since people once pointed to their nose to mean "me."

etymologyHint: As busy as the market 市 gate 门

components.note: 门 (a door/gate) — the entrance.
市 (a market) — bustling with people, together giving 闹 its meaning 'noisy, to make a commotion.'

example.fact: 闹 commonly appears in 热闹 (rènao, "lively, bustling") and 闹钟 (nàozhōng, "alarm clock").

components.note: 羊 is a simple picture of a sheep's head, seen from the front, with two curved horns at the top.

example.pinyin: Cǎodì shàng yǒu hěn duō yáng.
example.english: There are many sheep on the grassland.
example.fact: 羊 covers both "sheep" and "goat" in everyday Chinese, and is also one of the twelve zodiac animals.

etymologyHint: One with wooden 木 speech 口

components.note: 口 (mouth) — someone's speech.
木 (wood) — stiff and unresponsive, together giving 呆 its meaning 'dull, blank, foolish.'

example.pinyin: Tā dāidāi de zhàn zài nàlǐ.
example.fact: 呆 commonly appears in 呆呆地 (dāidāi de, "blankly, in a daze") and 发呆 (fādāi, "to space out").

example.english: The teacher is very strict with students.
example.fact: 厉 commonly appears in 严厉 (yánlì, "strict, severe") and 厉害 (lìhài, "amazing, terrific").

etymologyHint: A big 大 horn 角; 行 provides the pronunciation

components.note: 角 (a horn) — a fixed point on a balance beam.
大 (big) — the wide crossbar of a scale itself, together giving 衡 its meaning 'to weigh, to measure, balance.'

example.hanzi: 我们要平衡工作和生活。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen yào pínghéng gōngzuò hé shēnghuó.
example.english: We need to balance work and life.
example.fact: 衡 almost always appears in 平衡 (pínghéng, "balance") and 衡量 (héngliáng, "to weigh, assess").

components.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — 胞 relates to the body, originally the womb.
包 (bāo) is an exact match for the sound of 胞.

example.fact: 胞 commonly appears in 同胞 (tóngbāo, "fellow countryman, compatriot") and 细胞 (xìbāo, "cell," the biological unit).

components.note: 雨 (rain) — 零 originally described light, scattered rain, extended to mean a fragment or zero.
令 (lìng) is an exact match for the sound of 零, differing only in tone.

example.fact: 零 is the character for "zero," as in 零度 (líng dù, "zero degrees") and 零食 (língshí, "snacks").

example.english: His family used to be poor.
example.fact: 穷 is the basic word for "poor," the opposite of 富 (fù, "rich").

components.note: 人 (person) — 舍 originally described the shape of a roof over a person, a dwelling.
舌 (shé) is an exact match for the sound of 舍.

example.english: He can't bear to leave home.
example.fact: 舍 commonly appears in 舍不得 (shěbudé, "to be reluctant to part with") and 宿舍 (sùshè, "dormitory").

components.note: 石 (stone) — 码 originally related to counting stones used for reckoning, extended to mean 'number, code.'
马 (mǎ) is an exact match for the sound of 码.

example.pinyin: Qǐng gàosu wǒ nǐ de hàomǎ.
example.fact: 码 commonly appears in 号码 (hàomǎ, "number") and 密码 (mìmǎ, "password").

meanings: abbr. for 赫茲|赫兹[he4 zi1], hertz (Hz)
etymologyHint: Blushing 赤 bright red 赤

components.note: 赫 shows 赤 (red) twice, side by side — an intense, blazing red or glow, giving 赫 its meaning 'bright, radiant, illustrious.'

example.hanzi: 他是一位赫赫有名的科学家。
example.pinyin: Tā shì yí wèi hèhè yǒumíng de kēxuéjiā.
example.english: He is a very famous scientist.
example.fact: 赫 commonly appears in 显赫 (xiǎnhè, "illustrious, prominent") and as the transliteration for "hertz," the unit of frequency (赫兹, hèzī).

components.note: 女 (woman) — 婆 names an older woman.
波 (bō) gives a sound close to pó, sharing the same rhyme.

example.fact: 婆 commonly appears in 外婆 (wàipó, "maternal grandmother") and 婆婆 (pópo, "husband's mother, mother-in-law").

components.note: 鬼 (ghost/spirit) — 魂 names a person's spirit or soul.
云 (yún) gives a rhyme close to hún, with a different initial.

example.english: Chinese people believe people have souls.
example.fact: 魂 almost always appears in 灵魂 (línghún, "soul, spirit") in everyday speech.

etymologyHint: A house 宀 on fire 火

components.note: 宀 (a roof) — a house.
火 (fire) — burning inside it, together giving 灾 its meaning 'disaster, calamity.'

example.english: That fire disaster was very serious.
example.fact: 灾 commonly appears in 火灾 (huǒzāi, "fire disaster") and 灾难 (zāinàn, "catastrophe, disaster").

etymologyHint: All 共 the water 氵; 共 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 氵 (water) — the flood itself.
共 (together, combined) — many streams joining into one overwhelming flow, together giving 洪 its meaning 'flood, vast.'

example.english: A flood happened here last year.
example.fact: 洪 almost always appears in 洪水 (hóngshuǐ, "flood") in everyday speech.

etymologyHint: Flesh ⺼ used to walk 退; 退 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — part of the body.
退 (to step back, retreat) — used to move and walk, together giving 腿 its meaning 'leg.'

example.fact: 腿 is the basic word for "leg," as in 大腿 (dàtuǐ, "thigh") and 桌腿 (zhuōtuǐ, "table leg").

components.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — 胆 names a body organ, the gallbladder.
旦 (dàn) gives a sound close to dǎn, differing only in tone.

example.english: He has a lot of courage.
example.fact: 胆 commonly appears in 胆量 (dǎnliàng, "courage, guts") and 胆小 (dǎnxiǎo, "timid, cowardly").

meanings: abbr. for Tianjin 天津[Tian1 jin1]

components.note: 氵 (water) — 津 names a place to cross water, a ferry crossing.
聿 (yù) gives a sound distantly related to jīn, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 天津是中国的一个城市。
example.pinyin: Tiānjīn shì Zhōngguó de yí gè chéngshì.
example.english: Tianjin is a city in China.
example.fact: 津 is best known today as part of 天津 (Tiānjīn), a major city near Beijing, and in 津津有味 (jīnjīn yǒuwèi, "with relish").

components.note: 亻 (person) — 俗 relates to people's shared customs.
谷 (gǔ) gives a sound distantly related to sú, having drifted apart over time.

example.hanzi: 每个地方都有自己的风俗。
example.pinyin: Měi gè dìfang dōu yǒu zìjǐ de fēngsú.
example.english: Every place has its own customs.
example.fact: 俗 commonly appears in 风俗 (fēngsú, "custom, tradition") and 通俗 (tōngsú, "popular, common").

etymologyHint: A bitter 辛 exchange of words 讠

components.note: 讠 (speech, words) — the middle of the character, an exchange of talk.
辛 (bitter, sharp), placed on both sides, representing the two disputing parties, together giving 辩 its meaning 'to argue, debate.'

example.fact: 辩 commonly appears in 辩论 (biànlùn, "to debate") and 辩护 (biànhù, "to defend, plead").

etymologyHint: A heart ⺼ in the chest 匈; 匈 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: ⺼ (flesh/body) — part of the body.
匈 here representing an enclosed cavity, together giving 胸 its meaning 'chest, breast.'

example.fact: 胸 commonly appears in 胸口 (xiōngkǒu, "chest") and 胸怀 (xiōnghuái, "breadth of mind, aspiration").

components.note: 日 (sun) — 晓 describes the sun coming up, dawn, and by extension, becoming clear.
尧 (yáo) gives a sound close to xiǎo.

example.pinyin: Tā bù zhīxiǎo zhè jiàn shì.
example.english: He doesn't know about this matter.
example.fact: 晓 commonly appears in 知晓 (zhīxiǎo, "to know, be aware of") and 拂晓 (fúxiǎo, "dawn").

components.note: 力 (strength) — 劲 names physical strength or energy.

example.english: He has a lot of strength.
example.fact: 劲 commonly appears in 有劲 (yǒujìn, "to have strength/energy") and 使劲 (shǐjìn, "to exert effort").

etymologyHint: Money 贝 that must be split 分; 分 also provides the pronunciation

components.note: 分 (to divide, split) — resources split too thin.
贝 (money, originally shells used as currency) — too little to go around, together giving 贫 its meaning 'poor, needy.'

example.fact: 贫 commonly appears in 贫穷 (pínqióng, "poor") and 贫富 (pínfù, "poor and rich").

etymologyHint: A caring relationship between two 二 people 亻

components.note: 亻 (person) — one person.
二 (two) — a second person, together showing a caring relationship between two people, giving 仁 its meaning 'humaneness, benevolence.'

example.pinyin: Tā shì yí gè hěn réncí de rén.
example.english: He is a very kind person.
example.fact: 仁 commonly appears in 仁慈 (réncí, "kind, benevolent") and is a core concept in Confucian philosophy, meaning "humaneness, benevolence."
